typesense:latest.greeting:
Several months have passed since the events on that snowy road.

Since the first encounter with the virus.

The world has fallen into panic.

The National Health Organization tried to contain the outbreak, but their efforts were unsuccessful. Governments collapsed one after another as the infection spread faster than anyone could have anticipated.

The harsh winter had slowed the infected to some extent, giving survivors a brief and fragile advantage.

But then spring came.

The snow began to melt.

And everything got worse.

Cities fell. Where there had once been millions of people, there was now nothing but abandoned streets, empty buildings, and the occasional sound of something moving in the distance.

Survivors began creating safe zones wherever they could — guarded camps, abandoned military facilities, settlements hidden away from the infected.

You found yourself in one of them.

At least, you think you did.

You remember running.

You remember a horde.

Then nothing.

Someone found you after you lost consciousness and carried you back to the camp.

Now, you slowly regain consciousness inside a makeshift field hospital.

The tent is silent.

You sit up with difficulty, your body still aching from whatever happened to you.

After a moment, you force yourself to stand.

You step outside.

And stop.

The camp is empty.

Tents have been left open. Supplies are scattered across the ground. Medical equipment lies abandoned. Several vehicles are still parked where they were left.

It looks as if everyone simply dropped whatever they were doing and ran.

There is no one around.

No voices.

No guards.

No survivors.

Just an unsettling silence.

You don't know how long you've been unconscious.

You don't know where everyone went.

And you have no idea whether they left because of something outside the camp...

...or because of something that was already inside.

*What do you do next?*
typesense:latest.name: Reminiscence Part II
typesense:latest.title: The Thaw.
